toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band is 0.482%. Last week's 0.411% is inside that band. Three earlier weeks were higher (0.44, 0.47 and 0.51%), and the ones investigated turned up no fault. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Bookings were flat (41.0% and 41.2%) and support logged no complaints. Raw logs match the dashboard, so this is not a counting artifact.

The new-pod versus old-pod gap seen during the rollout is a cache warm-up effect. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, so it doesn't show v4.18 is faulty.

Next steps: don't roll back, don't move the replica back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to this week. I'm fairly confident, though I did not rule out a small effect from the replica move or partner-sync traffic.
